newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian govt reaches agreement on 97 budget-source.
newsitem.headline: Belgian govt reaches agreement on 97 budget-source.

text.p: The Belgian government has reached full agreement on its 1997 budget, a government source told Reuters on Friday.
The budget target is to cut the total public deficit to 2.9 percent of GDP in 1997 from an estimated 3.0 percent in 1996. The total austerity package is worth 80 billion francs, the source said.
The source said 30 billion francs would come from higher taxes -- mainly indirect -- while 50 billion francs would come from spending cuts in the social security sector.

The non-indexation of income tax rates and the gains the central bank expects to book on a renewal of 100-franc bills will contribute to cutting the deficit to 2.9 percent, but is not accounted for in the 80 billion franc package.
The source said banks would have to pay a 0.6 percent turnover tax on savings books accounts, the tax-free regulated savings accounts which are Belgium's most popular savings instrument.
